title: Grateful Dead Live at Haight Street on 1968-03-03
lineage: AUD > ?? > CD > EAC > CD Wave > SHN

ai_review.summary: A gritty audience recording that nonetheless captures the legendary flat‑bed truck show’s soaring Viola Lee Blues and fiery blues jams.
ai_review.review: The tape is an audience capture – not a soundboard – with limited fidelity, occasional drop‑outs and battery‑powered hiss, but it preserves the historic free‑show vibe. Musically the performance shines: a monster 20‑minute “Viola Lee” and extended versions of Pigpen’s blues staples (Smokestack Lightning, Lovelight, Hurts Me Too) are repeatedly praised, making this a must‑hear for early‑Dead fans.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars and highlight standout jams; recording is acknowledged as rough but acceptable, yielding a solid overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: No soundboard; recorded by a fan with limited battery power – occasional hiss, drop‑outs and reduced clarity, but better than many other early 1968 audience tapes.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Impromptu, free‑street gig on Haight with flatbed trucks; heavy blues jam focus, high energy, historic stage banter and crowd excitement keep the flow lively despite a repetitive feel in places.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mentioned as embodying freedom; his guitar drives the intense Viola Lee jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass described as distinct and almost magical during the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Takes over vocals on Lovelight later in the set, a point noted as less attractive by one reviewer.
